turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come through. I'll put your observations in before the doctor calls you. Temperature's thirty seven point two, pulse is eighty eight, and your blood pressure is one twenty eight over seventy six.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that alright? It feels like my heart's racing. Is eighty eight too quick, and is that blood pressure high?
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Both of those are fine from where I'm standing. Doctor won't be a minute. There's a sample pot if you can wee.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I tried in the loo and it was only a dribble. Sorry. I get really embarrassed about this.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's been putting it off. I had to nag her all morning to come down to the surgery.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Okonkwo. Have a seat. What's been happening?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the burning when I wee, again. It really stings, and I need to go all the time, even when hardly anything comes out.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's been up half the night with it. Started three days ago, on Wednesday.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Mum, that's not right. It was Sunday night, so two days. You always make it longer than it is.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): You're not quite agreeing, so I'm going to think of it as roughly two to three days. Any blood in the wee?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood, I looked. I don't feel feverish either, and my back doesn't hurt. I just feel a bit washed out, that's all.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She said earlier this is the third time this year.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Third... well, actually, maybe the fourth. January, March, June, and now. Is four a lot? Am I ruining my kidneys?

[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Four in a year is more than I'd want, I'm not going to dress that up, but it doesn't mean your kidneys are being damaged. These usually sit in the bladder. Have you already taken something?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I was too embarrassed to ring again, so I took my sister's leftover antibiotic. Nitrofurantoin capsules.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): What strength, and how often? I need the actual amount, not a guess if you can help it.

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, the nitrofurantoin, by mouth. A hundred milligrams, I think twice a day, for the stinging. I had three days of them. Maybe it was fifty milligrams. No, a hundred. I'm not sure I took every dose.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She skipped the middle day. I saw the capsules still on the side. They were Chloe's, from last winter. I did say not to.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I took most of them. They ran out yesterday, so I've stopped. Does that wreck the urine test? Will it still show an infection?

[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): It can muddy the result, yes. I'm thinking it through out loud. If the nitrofurantoin has knocked the bacteria back, the culture may not grow anything even if this is still a urine infection. We'll send a sample anyway.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): So there is a test? How long does that take? And are you going to give me more antibiotics, because I don't want to take the wrong thing.

[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): A dipstick while you're here, and the lab culture is usually back in a couple of days. I'm not prescribing another antibiotic this afternoon. We might, if something grows that needs treating. Any discharge, itching, or soreness down below?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. Sorry, it's mortifying even being asked.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): I know, and I still have to be precise. No discharge at all?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Well... actually, there has been a bit. Creamy, for a couple of days. Not much. No itching, though. I didn't want to say it out loud.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She told me yesterday the discharge was quite a lot, not a bit. And she's gone off her food and feels sick with it.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not true. I had toast this morning and I don't feel sick. It's only a little discharge. Why say it like that?
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll put down that you disagree on the amount, and on the nausea. What I can check myself is more use. Let me feel your tummy.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Abdomen's soft, nothing tender over the bladder, and your loins aren't sore when I tap them. That's reassuring against a kidney infection.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): So it's not my kidneys? Could the discharge be thrush? I had thrush once, years ago. And can I go to work tomorrow?

[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Kidneys feel unlikely on this exam. Thrush is possible next to a cystitis, I'm not ready to call it that. Work is fine if you feel up to it. Keep drinking water, and please don't borrow anyone else's tablets again.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): What if the burning's worse tonight? Do I come back here or go to A and E? And is thirty seven point two nearly a temperature?

[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thirty seven point two is not a fever. If you get shivers, vomiting, or pain in the back, A and E is the right place. Otherwise, if it's not settling in three days, come back to us.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Three days sounds ages when it stings. Will somebody ring me about the culture? What if I still can't wee in the pot?
[SEG0035] person_1 (NURSE): I'll sort a pot and a bit of privacy after this. Midstream if you can manage it, just the middle of the wee. We dip it here and send the rest off.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, dipstick and a culture, that's the order. I'm treating this as another bout of cystitis for now, and thrush is something I can't rule out because of that discharge.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): But the nitrofurantoin won't hide it completely, will it? I'm really worried this becomes a fifth time. Should I be scared?

[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): It might partly hide it, that's the honest bit, so a negative culture wouldn't fully clear you. Come back if it's not settling in three days, and sooner if you feel properly unwell.
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll make sure she actually gets in touch if it turns. She won't, if it's left to her.
